title: Microsoft Dataverse: management MCP server for building and governing MCP servers

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: Microsoft has not confirmed that the Dataverse environment switch or client allow list governs the separate management endpoint, so administrators cannot rely on the stated protection. The default contradicts the roadmap, an admin documentation link returns 404, and automation for the Dataverse client allow list is incorrectly reported as undocumented.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP availability settings are under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol.
claims.quote: Select the Environment Name where you want to turn on the Dataverse MCP server, and then select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. Scroll down to locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row, allowed MCP clients
claims.claim: The first row's path also gives the complete location for configuring allowed MCP clients.
claims.quote:
Select Advanced Settings.
The list of available clients is shown. Open the client record you want.
On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.
claims.fix: Split availability and client configuration into separate rows. For clients, extend the current path with "Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled"; for availability name "Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server". Keep both explicitly limited to the Dataverse data endpoint.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for the first row's Dataverse MCP client allow list.
claims.quote: Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment. This command is an alternative to the manual admin step
claims.fix: For a separate Dataverse allowed-client row, document the preview CLI command "dataverse mcp allow <appId>" (kind "other"), citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/cli/reference. State that Dataverse admin permissions are required; do not extend its scope to MCPManagement.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row; sources
claims.claim: The cited Microsoft 365 Copilot URL documents Agents > Tools > Registry > tool > Block for controlling MCP tools.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "Agents" "Tools" "Registry" "Block" Microsoft 365 admin. Cited /microsoft-365/copilot/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers returned HTTP 404; opened the replacement /microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers.
claims.fix: Replace the docs/source URL with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. Describe "Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block" as whole-server blocking for registered servers. Individual tools use "MCP server > Tools > tool toggle" only on supported server types through the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway; do not imply this governs every direct management-endpoint call.

claims.claim: No equivalent command or API is documented for the Microsoft 365 admin center MCP blocking control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365" "MCP" tools block PowerShell Graph API; "Agent 365" "MCP" "block" "Graph API". Opened the moved management page and develop-mcp reference; the latter says its block command was removed and directs admins to the admin center.

claims.claim: A data policy can be created through Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select Security, and then on the Security pane, select Data and privacy.
On the Data protection and privacy page, select Data policy.
Select an existing policy on the command bar and then select Edit policy, or select New Policy to create a new policy to configure.

-Environments

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth row; Open questions
claims.claim: A dedicated administrative UI or automation setting for controlling access to the management MCP server itself is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCPManagement" "permissions" "admin"; "MCPManagement" "disable"; "management MCP server" "enabled". Opened mcp-management, data-platform-mcp-disable and develop-mcp; no dedicated management-endpoint enable/disable control was documented.

claims.claim: The management MCP server inherits the Dataverse MCP server's environment switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "management MCP" "DLP" "Dataverse" allowlist; "management MCP server" "enabled". Opened mcp-management and data-platform-mcp-disable: the former has an agent365.svc.cloud.microsoft endpoint; neither states that it inherits the Dataverse switch.
claims.fix: Remove the inheritance assertion. Say: "Microsoft has not confirmed that the Dataverse MCP environment switch governs the management MCP endpoint." Add that qualification to the Dataverse control row.

claims.claim: The management MCP server inherits the Dataverse MCP client allow list.
claims.quote: Searched: "management MCP" "DLP" "Dataverse" allowlist. Opened mcp-management and data-platform-mcp-disable. The latter limits MCP allow listing to /api/mcp; no passage applies that list to the distinct MCPManagement endpoint.
claims.fix: Remove the inheritance assertion. State that the cited Dataverse documentation limits client allow listing to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint and does not establish protection of the separate management endpoint.

claims.claim: A tenant permitting Dataverse MCP for one purpose also permits the management MCP server.
claims.quote: Searched: "management MCP server" "access" "control"; "management MCP server" "enabled". Opened mcp-management, data-platform-mcp-disable and the moved admin management page. None establishes that Dataverse permission grants management-server access.
claims.fix: Delete this conclusion and the assertion that admin tooling makes no distinction. Replace them with: "Do not assume that allowing or blocking the Dataverse data endpoint grants or revokes access to the management endpoint; Microsoft has not documented that relationship."

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can block whole MCP servers.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: This management-server change has a confirmed metered cost, as asserted by the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCPManagement" licensing credits management server; "Dataverse" "management MCP server" "licensing". Read mcp-management and Copilot Studio billing-licensing results. General agent billing is documented, but no meter for this management capability is stated.
claims.fix: Set cost to "low" for known administration effort and start the cost rationale "Low. Administration effort; licensing for the management server is not yet published." Keep consuming-agent charges explicitly conditional and separate from any unconfirmed management-server meter.

claims.claim: Consuming agents may incur Copilot Credits charges.
claims.quote: By using the pay-as-you-go meter, at the end of each month, your organization pays only for the actual number of Copilot Credits its agents use during the month.
claims.fix: Add this billing source and specify "Copilot Studio consuming agents may use Copilot Credits under their existing billing model; this does not establish a charge for the management server."

claims.claim: Underlying premium connector use has licensing considerations.
claims.quote: The standalone Copilot Studio subscription lets you build agents on any supported channel and connect to any data using premium connectors.
claims.fix: Add this licensing source and keep the statement conditional on the consuming product and licence. Do not imply that a premium connector necessarily requires a separate add-on beyond the consuming product's existing rights.

claims.claim: Underlying Dataverse API use can be subject to API limits.
claims.quote: Dataverse evaluates service protection API limits for each user. Each authenticated user has an independent limit.
claims.fix: Cite this API-limits page and describe the limits as constraints on underlying Dataverse calls, not as a published management-server quota or pricing meter.
